input.purpose: Measure V_lab, the air volume served by /habitat/lab/eclss/scrubber-1-v8, from the CO2 rise and full-speed decay time constant.
hypotheses: The closed /habitat/lab/hatch-1-v8 keeps the Lab as one well-mixed zone throughout both phases.
Unmeasured air exchange through the closed hatch is small and constant enough not to dominate the fitted decay; the Hab-B CO2 record is used to challenge this hypothesis.
FE-1 remains in the Lab at steady activity for the whole test, so occupant CO2 generation is steady.
The scrubber effective flow follows its accepted speed command, and the registered full-speed effective flow is applicable.
The engineering first guess is a 30 min time constant; each phase therefore lasts one guessed time constant.
Fit the full-speed record to C(t) = C_eq + (C_0 - C_eq) exp(-t/tau), then calculate V_lab = Qe * tau; do not fit toward zero or outdoor concentration.

monitoring.reason: The test intentionally raises CO2 in the occupied Lab; monitoring starts only after commander authorisation.

steps.why: Hold the single-zone boundary and reduce effective flow so occupant-generated CO2 rises several hundred ppm above sensor noise; record Lab and Hab-B CO2, command acceptance, speed, occupancy and activity every minute.
Keep the same boundary and source, return to full speed, and record the equilibrium-offset decay every minute for the time-constant fit.

abort.when: Lab CO2 reaches or exceeds limits.co2AbortPpm.
The device refuses either commanded speed.
Scrubber battery state of charge is below threshold percent.
FE-1 is outside the specified heart-rate band, monitoring is lost, or any additional person enters the Lab.

expected.rise: At 30% speed, Lab CO2 should rise by several hundred ppm without exceeding 2800 ppm; failure to rise clearly above noise challenges the source or speed-response hypotheses.
expected.decay: At 100% speed, Lab CO2 should follow a monotonic exponential approach to a nonzero fitted equilibrium with an estimated time constant near 30 min.
expected.volume: Fit tau from the full-speed phase and report V_lab = Qe * tau in m3 using the scrubber's registered full-speed effective flow.
expected.openingCheck: Hab-B CO2 should not track the Lab transient strongly. Correlated convergence or a changing Lab/Hab-B gradient challenges the negligible closed-hatch exchange hypothesis and invalidates a single-zone volume result.
expected.validity: Any occupancy change, activity change, command refusal, non-exponential decay, insufficient rise above noise, limit/abort event, or strong connected-zone response invalidates the volume fit.
